sections.title: Moses' First Speech
sections.description: Historical review of the wilderness journey and exhortation to obedience

sections.title: Moses' Second Speech
sections.description: The law repeated and expanded with commands, statutes, and rights

sections.title: Renewal of the Covenant
sections.description: The covenant is renewed with blessings and curses, a call to choose life

sections.title: Farewell and Moses' Death
sections.description: Joshua is appointed, Moses' song and blessing, Moses' death on Mount Nebo

events.title: Moses Begins His Speech
events.description: On the plains of Moab, east of the Jordan, Moses begins to explain the law to all Israel. It is the fortieth year after leaving Egypt, and the people stand at the border of the promised land. Moses gathers the people to prepare them for what lies ahead.

events.title: Review of the Wilderness Journey
events.description: Moses gives a detailed account of Israel's journey from Horeb to the plains of Moab. He reminds them of the spies' report, the people's disobedience at Kadesh-Barnea, the forty years in the wilderness, and victories over Sihon and Og east of the Jordan.

events.title: Exhortation to Obedience
events.description: Moses earnestly exhorts the people to keep God's commands and statutes. He reminds them that they saw with their own eyes what the Lord did at Baal-Peor. Moses warns against idolatry and emphasizes that the Lord is a jealous God who demands faithfulness.

events.title: The Ten Commandments Repeated
events.description: Moses repeats the Ten Commandments to the new generation, which was not present at Horeb. He stresses that the covenant was made not only with their ancestors but with everyone living today. The people heard God's voice from the midst of the fire and asked Moses to be their mediator.

events.title: "Hear, O Israel" - Shema
events.description: Moses proclaims the great commandment: "Hear, O Israel! The Lord our God, the Lord is one. You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength." These words are to be bound as a sign, written on the doorposts, and taught to children in every situation of life.

events.title: Israel as God's Chosen People
events.description: Moses explains that the Lord did not choose Israel because they were the greatest nation, but because He loved them and kept the oath He swore to their ancestors. He exhorts them to keep the covenant and promises that God will bless them with fertility and health if they are obedient.

events.title: The Main Content of the Law
events.description: Moses presents the central law code that is to apply in the promised land. It includes the place of worship the Lord will choose, rules for tithes, dietary laws, sabbatical years, the three major festivals, righteous judges, and regulations concerning prophets, cities, war, and social responsibility.

events.title: The Promise of a Prophet Like Moses
events.description: Moses proclaims that the Lord will raise up a prophet from among the people, like himself, whom they must listen to. This prophecy was later understood as a messianic promise. God will put His words in this prophet's mouth.

events.title: Blessings and Curses
events.description: Moses sets forth the detailed blessings that follow obedience and the extensive curses that follow disobedience. The blessings include fertility, victory, and prosperity. The curses are far more elaborate and warn of disease, defeat, captivity, and destruction if the people break the covenant.

events.title: Renewal of the Covenant on the Plains of Moab
events.description: Moses renews the covenant between the Lord and Israel on the plains of Moab, in addition to the covenant at Horeb. He places before the people the decisive choice: "I have set before you life and death, blessing and curse. Choose life, so that you and your descendants may live!"

events.title: Joshua Appointed as Leader
events.description: Moses is 120 years old and can no longer lead the people. He announces that Joshua will lead the people across the Jordan. Moses calls Joshua forward in front of all Israel and says: "Be strong and courageous! You shall lead this people into the land that the Lord has sworn to give their fathers."

events.title: Moses' Song
events.description: Moses delivers a powerful song for all Israel as a witness against the people. The song praises God's greatness and faithfulness, while warning of the people's future unfaithfulness. It prophesies about apostasy, God's judgment, and finally His mercy toward His people.

events.title: Moses Blesses the Tribes
events.description: Before his death, Moses pronounces a blessing over each of Israel's twelve tribes, similar to Jacob's blessing in Genesis. Each tribe receives a prophetic blessing tailored to their character and future. The song concludes with praise to God as Israel's refuge and help.

events.title: Moses' Death on Mount Nebo
events.description: Moses goes up Mount Nebo, and the Lord shows him all the promised land from Gilead to Dan, Naphtali, Ephraim, Manasseh, Judah all the way to the sea, and the Negev. Moses dies there in the land of Moab according to the word of the Lord, 120 years old. No one knows his grave. Israel mourns for thirty days, and it is stated that never again has a prophet arisen in Israel like Moses.
